title: CGAP: Filipino Financial Customers' Views on Empowerment (public source)
summary: CGAP focus groups and interviews with low-income financial customers in Metro Manila, Rizal and Bulacan on choosing providers, using services (including ATMs and digital services) and speaking up.

population.segment: Low-income financial customers, mostly microfinance clients

label_notes: Pages are 1-based PDF page indexes. Sample = 51 FGD participants + 12 unique interviewees (p.2). Fieldwork dates are not stated; the report date (May 2015) is used as fieldwork_end and should be confirmed. Theme texts avoid stating incidence, as the assistant requires for qualitative evidence; the report's own percentages are in the quotes.

findings.text: Participants described comparing providers and asking friends about their experience before choosing where to borrow; a few felt unable to make informed choices.
findings.quote: I shop around FSPs for terms that are easy and affordable

findings.text: Participants described a borrowing path from family and friends to informal moneylenders, and wanting to stop using moneylenders once they had a formal provider because of the high rates.
findings.quote: many customers expressed a wish to stop taking loans from informal moneylenders because of their usurious rates

findings.text: Participants who used digital financial services had mostly started through government programmes such as 4Ps or through employers, not by their own choice.
findings.quote: customers with experience in remittances became DFS users not by personal choice but through their affiliation with government programs

findings.text: Participants said they learned to use ATMs from family members, friends or the branch security guard, and rarely used telephone hotlines.
findings.quote: Security guard—ever present and available, the guard usually becomes the source of information on how to use the ATM

findings.text: Participants said they would rather leave a provider that serves them poorly than complain, believing one voice cannot change how institutions work.
findings.quote: Filipinos, being generally non-confrontational, would rather just leave than have their individual voices heard

findings.text: I was accompanied by my niece when I first withdrew money using my ATM card. She was my teacher.
findings.quote: I was accompanied by my niece when I first withdrew money using my ATM card. She was my teacher.

findings.text: Hard life and cash shortage keeps me borrowing money. I hope that I will not be in debt forever.
findings.quote: Hard life and cash shortage keeps me borrowing money. I hope that I will not be in debt forever.

findings.text: I am only one voice; to be heard, there may be a need for a collective voice.
findings.quote: I am only one voice; to be heard, there may be a need for a collective voice.
